title: An optimized protocol to isolate quiescent washed platelets from human whole blood and generate platelet releasate under clinical conditions
protocol: Collect 30–40 mL blood per donor/patient via venepuncture with a 21-gauge needle into individual 10 mL acid citrate dextrose-a (ACD-A) vacutainer tubes.
Discard the first 5 mL of blood as platelets will be activated through shear stress.
Gently invert the blood collection tubes to ensure even distribution of the anticoagulant.
Centrifuge blood samples at 200 × g at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 15 min with no brake to generate platelet rich plasma (PRP).
Disable the brake function of the centrifuge.
Transfer the upper layer containing PRP into a conical 50 mL falcon tube.
Add 1 μM PGE1 (1 μL of a 10 mM stock per 10 mL of PRP) to the PRP and gently invert the tube once.
Leave behind 5 mm PRP above the buffy coat to prevent white and red blood cell contamination.
Adjust the pH of the PRP to 6.5 with ACD-A.
Add ACD-A dropwise to the PRP and carefully invert platelets once.
Centrifuge blood samples at 150 × g at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 7 min with brake set to 4.
Transfer the supernatant into a fresh 50 mL falcon tube, add 1 μM PGE1, and gently invert tube.
Centrifuge PRP at 600 × g at room temperature (20°C–25°C) with brake set to 4 for 10 min to pellet platelets.
Remove supernatant (platelet poor plasma (PPP)).
Wash the platelet pellet by carefully resuspending them in 10 mL Modified Tyrode’s buffer.
Use a disposable transfer pipette for resuspension of platelets.
Re-centrifuge platelets as in step 7.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Determine platelet concentration using an automated cell counter.
Resuspend platelets to a final concentration of 1 × 10^9 platelets/mL in Modified Tyrode’s buffer.
Rest platelets for 15 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
The platelets can now be used for follow-up experiments such as the ADP release assay or proteomics analysis.
Add 1.8 mM CaCl2 to the platelet suspension.
Leave platelets to re-calcify for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aliquot 450 μL of platelets into aggregation tubes.
Prewarm platelets to 37°C for at least 5 min.
Place aggregation tube into the aggregometer.
Establish a baseline for 10 seconds.
Add 50 μL agonist directly into the aggregation tube using gel-loading tips or similar.
Let reaction run for 5 minutes.
Place aggregation tubes immediately on ice after 5 min of aggregation.
Transfer contents of the aggregation tube into a precooled microcentrifuge tube using a micropipette.
Immediately add 10 μL of both protease and phosphatase inhibitors to the microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 μL PGE1 (10 mM stock) to the microcentrifuge tube.
Leave microcentrifuge tubes on ice until all samples have been processed.
Centrifuge samples at 1,000 × g and 4°C for 10 min.
Carefully remove supernatant and transfer into a fresh pre-cooled microcentrifuge tube making sure not to disturb the platelet clot.
Leave about 20 μL above the clot to prevent platelet contamination of the PR.
Optionally, discard or wash and lyse the platelet pellet on ice for 60 min using a suitable precooled lysis buffer and store at −80°C for further analysis.
Repeat steps for a total of 3 centrifugations.
After the final spin, add 10 μL protease inhibitors to the PR.
Add 10 μL phosphatase inhibitors to the PR.
Add 1 μL PGE1 (10 mM stock) to the PR.
Store enriched PR at −80°C until further use.
